learning: Iteration 9 showed that lowering the radius to 0.025 m reduced progress on every track without fixing max_error or line loss. Speed appears to be a binding limit, so the next test goes upward.
notes: Iteration 8 geometry and controller with wheel_radius raised to 0.034 m, the only change. This isolates the ground-speed effect that iteration 9 showed in the opposite direction.
rationale: The Builder's geometry changes only wheel_radius, from 0.030 m (iteration 8) to 0.034 m. Iteration 9 cut the radius to 0.025 m, and the score fell 1.65 with progress lower on all three tracks (oval 0.197 vs 0.201, s-bend 0.185 vs 0.188, slalom 0.119 vs 0.125). max_error and line loss did not improve. Speed is therefore not too high, so a larger radius is the direction the evidence supports. The controller stays identical to iteration 8 (kp 1.25, ki 0, kd 0.30, base_speed 1.5, the seven-sensor weights [2.0, 1.3, 0.7, 0, -0.7, -1.3, -2.0], last_direction). Changing gains now would confound the speed test. I expect progress to rise on the oval and s-bend, with max_error near 0.062-0.066 m and steering oscillation close to iteration 8 values. Any drift in oscillation will show whether the faster ground speed needs more damping in a later iteration.
